The Taylor series about $x=0$ for a certain function $f$ converges to $f(x)$ for all $x$ in the interval of convergence. The $n$th derivative of $f$ at $x=0$ is given by
$$
f^{(n)}(0)=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(n+1)!}{5^{n}(n-1)^{2}} \text { for } n \geq 2
$$

The graph of $f$ has a horizontal tangent line at $x=0$, and $f(0)=6$.\\
(a) Determine whether $f$ has a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at $x=0$. Justify your answer.\\
(b) Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial for $f$ about $x=0$.\\
(c) Find the radius of convergence of the Taylor series for $f$ about $x=0$. Show the work that leads to your answer.

\section*{Question 3}

The Taylor series about \(x=0\) for a certain function \(f\) converges to \(f(x)\) for all \(x\) in the interval of convergence. The \(n\)th derivative of \(f\) at \(x=0\) is given by
\[
f^{(n)}(0)=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(n+1)!}{5^{n}(n-1)^{2}} \text { for } n \geq 2 .
\]
The graph of \(f\) has a horizontal tangent line at \(x=0\), and \(f(0)=6\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Determine whether \(f\) has a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at \(x=0\). Justify your answer.
\item[(b)] Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial for \(f\) about \(x=0\).
\item[(c)] Find the radius of convergence of the Taylor series for \(f\) about \(x=0\). Show the work that leads to your answer.
\item[(a)] \(f\) has a relative maximum at \(x=0\) because \(f^{\prime}(0)=0\) and \(f^{\prime \prime}(0)<0\).
\item[(b)] \(\quad f(0)=6, f^{\prime}(0)=0\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime \prime}(0)=-\frac{3!}{5^{2} 1^{2}}=-\frac{6}{25}, f^{\prime \prime \prime}(0)=\frac{4!}{5^{3} 2^{2}} \\
& P(x)=6-\frac{3!x^{2}}{5^{2} 2!}+\frac{4!x^{3}}{5^{3} 2^{2} 3!}=6-\frac{3}{25} x^{2}+\frac{1}{125} x^{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(u_{n}=\frac{f^{(n)}(0)}{n!} x^{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(n+1)}{5^{n}(n-1)^{2}} x^{n}\)
\[
\begin{gathered}
\left|\frac{u_{n+1}}{u_{n}}\right|=\left|\frac{\frac{(-1)^{n+2}(n+2)}{5^{n+1} n^{2}} x^{n+1}}{\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(n+1)}{5^{n}(n-1)^{2}} x^{n}}\right| \\
=\left(\frac{n+2}{n+1}\right)\left(\frac{n-1}{n}\right)^{2} \frac{1}{5}|x| \\
\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty}\left|\frac{u_{n+1}}{u_{n}}\right|=\frac{1}{5}|x|<1 \text { if }|x|<5 .
\end{gathered}
\]
The radius of convergence is 5 .
\end{itemize}
